target_customer: Military and defense buyers in Ukraine, Europe and the USA needing wide-area tracking of drones and cruise missiles
problem: Radars are active, jammable, expensive and built to protect single assets, while drone swarms and stealthy low-altitude threats need persistent wide-area passive coverage at low cost.
business_model: Hardware sensor network plus software sold to defense customers (pricing not stated)
product_category: Defense hardware: passive distributed aerial threat tracking (Mentat)

founders.name: Deo Arlo
previous_startups: Makrverse (funded platform for commercializing inventions, outcome not stated)
Venture spun out from his patented Technion robotic invention (name not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Over six years in Israel during multiple conflicts.

competitors.name: Sky Fortress
competitors.what: Ukrainian acoustic sensor network feeding national air defense command and control
competitors.traction_then: Network detected about 84 incoming drones in one episode, all but four downed, per a US Army general

competitors.name: Zvook
competitors.what: AI passive acoustic early warning sensors
competitors.traction_then: Tested vehicle mounted at NATO BATT26 in Latvia
competitors.funding_then: Investment from DEPO Ventures Ukraine Fund (amount not found)

competitors.name: FENEK
competitors.what: Ukrainian acoustic detection of Shahed type drones and cruise missiles
competitors.traction_then: Detection ranges of 3 km for drones and 5 km for cruise missiles claimed

technical_complexity.rationale: Passive 3D tracking of small fast targets with a low-cost mesh needs sensing hardware, edge computer vision, mesh networking and field validation under contested conditions.

defensibility.rationale: Field-proven hardware and defense relationships are sticky once adopted, but acoustic and RF competitors are already fielded in Ukraine, and the company has shown no named contracts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals were fielding passive detection in Ukraine by 2026. No acquisition or copying of Arlo is reported.

market_need_then: Shahed drone attacks and the war in Ukraine created urgent demand for cheap persistent air defense sensing. A US Army article in April 2026 evaluated passive sensor networks in Ukraine.

branding.domain_note: Uses arlo1.com. The exact arlo.com belongs to Arlo Technologies, a consumer camera company.

identity.logo: Two logo files on the site, not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission statement driven: Air defence as a network, not a target; conflict should be concise and precise

branding.brand_signature: Founder as Iron Dome Guy persona on YC listings
branding.community_and_virality: A Product Hunt page with few followers and YC launch coverage. Search is dominated by Arlo Technologies cameras.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive founder story but a name that collides with a large consumer brand, with little independent press.

outcome_analysis: Arlo Industries is a Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founder has technical credentials and lived through Iron Dome era conflicts, and the company reports demonstrations with Ukrainian forces and partnerships in four countries, but no named contracts or funding amounts are public and passive acoustic competitors are already fielded.
notes: Founding year not stated in sources opened. VCBacked and Standout list pre-seed with Y Combinator as investor, no amount, so no round recorded. Location differs across sources (NYC on YC, Kyiv on site, SF and Troy NY in directories). Batch labels vary (S26, P26, X26). Sensing modality is stated as passive optical by one outlet and left unspecified on the YC page. Name origin not stated; the founder is listed as Deo Arlo. The recorded pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked) with no amount or confirmed date.
